transcript:
[00:00:00] Olivia Chen (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Olivia, AE at Redwood. with me is Diego, our solutions engineer.
[00:00:12] Maya Singh (CTO): Hi all, Maya here. thanks. we pulled Ben and Priya in to cover platform and security.
[00:00:18] Ben Carter: yep, Ben.
[00:00:20] Priya Rao: hi.
[00:00:22] Diego Marquez (SE): great. quick agenda - figure out integration surface: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, how you'd route through your gateway/proxy, rate limits, and what observability hooks you need. sound okay?
[00:00:33] Maya: sounds good. high level - Vertex has call routing and a per-tenant API gateway. we want an LLM layer for customer support triage and short-form responses, but it must go through our gateway and obey tenant quotas.
[00:00:45] Olivia: got it. are you thinking hosted first, or dedicated/private?
[00:00:50] Maya: I'd like to understand tradeoffs. we prefer hosted for speed to market but worried about data residency and guarantees. dedicated would give predictable throughput but is heavier.
[00:01:02] Diego: yep. typical pattern - start hosted for feature launch, then move to dedicated pools or private when you need isolation, VPC, or stricter controls. our SDKs and API are the same across modes, so integration work largely portable.
[00:01:16] Ben: quick technical Q - we've built a custom gateway that adds headers, rate-limits per-tenant, and does mutating transforms. can Redwood sit behind our proxy? we don't want to change that.
[00:01:28] Diego: yes, you can. we support routing through customer-managed proxies/gateways. you can present a single egress IP, or use per-tenant auth tokens. a couple caveats: keep-alive and streaming can be impacted by proxy timeouts, so we recommend long-lived connections and chunked streaming settings on the gateway.
[00:01:46] Priya: streaming is important for latency - customers expect near real-time chat. also we need token-level cost breakdowns and tracing to attribute spend.
[00:01:56] Olivia: we provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the Console and via APIs. for observability hooks, we have tracing headers you can propagate (x-redwood-trace-id) and we emit per-request traces to your account. are you using OpenTelemetry?
[00:02:10] Ben: yes, OTEL.
[00:02:12] Diego: perfect - we can push spans into your OTEL collector or expose traces in Console. we also support webhooks for events like model fallback or quota hits.
[00:02:23] Maya: what about SDKs? our team uses Python heavily and we've standardized on LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex for retrieval augmented generation.
[00:02:33] Diego: we have first-class Python and JS SDKs. additionally, we've published integration guides and sample repos for LangChain and LlamaIndex. for LlamaIndex we have examples for vector store connectors and retrieval prompts; for LangChain we have agent and chain examples.
[00:02:46] Olivia: I'll link the LangChain + LlamaIndex sample repo after the call.
[00:02:50] Priya: on the LlamaIndex example, does Redwood host embeddings or do we run our own vector store?
[00:02:56] Diego: you can do either. hosted embeddings + Redwood vector store is simplest; alternately you can use your own vector DB (Pinecone/Weaviate/FAISS) and call Redwood for generation. we provide batching and prefix caching which reduce cost for repeated context.
[00:03:14] Ben: batching - can you quantify? we have high concurrency but small prompts, so batching helps throughput but adds latency.
[00:03:22] Diego: batching is workload-aware; it groups requests up to configured max latency and batch size. typical wins are 20-40% token cost reduction for high small-request workloads, but you can tune to keep p95 latency within your SLO.
[00:03:36] Maya: security questions: SOC 2, KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO. Priya will need the security pack.
[00:03:44] Priya: yes, particularly around key management - we need to know if we can use our KMS or HSM for model encryption and key rotation, plus whether logs include raw prompts or hashed tokens.
[00:03:56] Olivia: for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS; hosted supports bring-your-own-key for certain contracts. audit logs include request metadata and full transcript options under higher retention tiers - we can redact if needed. we'll share the security pack.
[00:04:12] Ben: about quotas - can you enforce per-tenant quotas and rate limits?
[00:04:17] Diego: yes. Redwood has per-api-key quotas, rate-limiting tiers, and you can use our route tagging to attribute to tenants. since you run a gateway, you can also enforce upstream and pass through tokens. we recommend using short-lived tokens if you want stricter isolation.
[00:04:33] Maya: what about latency variance - some of our customers need <150ms p50 on short prompts. can Redwood meet that on hosted?
[00:04:42] Diego: depends on model and region. for small short-turn models and edge regions we can meet sub-150ms p50 on hosted; dedicated with pinned GPU pools gives more predictable p95. part of the POC is to run benchmarks with your prompts to measure p50/p95.
[00:04:58] Priya: do you support model variants or fallbacks? e.g., degrade to a smaller model if capacity is constrained.
[00:05:05] Olivia: yes - smart routing and automatic fallbacks are built-in. you can configure a policy: prefer low-cost model, but fallback to higher-capacity when latency exceeds threshold or error rates spike. we surface those events via webhooks and Console alerts.
[00:05:18] Ben: we have an internal policy that all PII is stripped at ingestion. does Redwood offer pre-ingestion redaction?
[00:05:25] Diego: we have optional pre-request filters you can run client-side or via gateway hooks; plus we offer on-the-fly redaction in Private deployments. for hosted we can work with your pipeline to scrub PII before it's stored.
[00:05:37] Maya: integration nitty-gritty - will existing telemetry from our gateway map to Redwood traces?
[00:05:43] Diego: yes, propagate the trace id; we've seen customers stitch gateway logs with Redwood traces to build full request timelines. we can provide a snippet that shows how to attach x-redwood-trace-id to requests.
[00:05:55] Priya: about rate-limits - if a tenant exceeds quota, what happens?
[00:05:59] Olivia: we can return 429s upstream, send webhook notifications, and optionally queue/buffer bursts via the dedicated autoscale burst option. the Queueing approach may add some latency but avoids wholesale failure.
[00:06:12] Ben: does Redwood support token throttling per route? we need per-route and per-tenant controls.
[00:06:16] Diego: yes - per-route quotas, per-api-key token budgets, and labels so you can split billing and trace usage.
[00:06:23] Maya: can you run within our VPC?
[00:06:26] Olivia: Dedicated and Private both support VPC peering or customer-managed VPCs for Private deployments; hosted is public but we offer enterprise arrangements with private networking for larger contracts.
[00:06:36] Ben: about SDK behaviour with proxies - we saw some weird chunking behaviour when using our gateway and another vendor. any recommendations?
[00:06:44] Diego: set the client to use streaming with smaller chunk sizes, ensure proxy doesn't buffer entire response, and set connection keep-alive. we'll share an example config for common proxies (envoy/nginx/Azure API Management).
[00:06:57] Maya: LangChain - can we use Redwood endpoints as a llm wrapper out of the box?
[00:07:02] Diego: yes, there is a LangChain LLM wrapper; we also have a Redwood native chain that supports function/tool calling and structured output. sample code will show connector usage with LlamaIndex nodes.
[00:07:13] Priya: about logging - can we get redaction at rest? we prefer not to store raw prompts long-term.
[00:07:19] Olivia: you can configure retention and redaction rules. by default hosted stores short retention; Dedicated/Private allow customer-managed retention and advanced redaction.
[00:07:28] Ben: any known limits with LlamaIndex or LangChain integrations?
[00:07:31] Diego: mostly around chunk sizes and prompt window - ensure your retriever provides relevant context. for large context we recommend our KV cache and chunked streaming. we have example notebooks showing embeddings batching and streaming responses to the client.
[00:07:45] Maya: licensing/compliance - are there export controls or restrictions for certain models?
[00:07:50] Olivia: some model licenses restrict commercial use; we maintain a curated model catalog and can advise on which models are suitable for your use case. we'll include a model-compatibility guide in the pack.
[00:08:01] Ben: operationally, if we need to instrument cost per-customer, does Redwood expose token costs per-request?
[00:08:07] Diego: yes - our usage APIs provide per-request token counts and cost estimates. you can tag requests for tenant attribution.
[00:08:14] Priya: we need a sample for the gateway that shows header propagation and short-lived token exchange.
[00:08:20] Diego: understood - I'll prepare a code sample that uses our token exchange flow and shows how to rotate tokens via your auth service.
[00:08:27] Maya: can Redwood run a POC with our traffic pattern?
[00:08:31] Olivia: yes - typical POC is 2-4 weeks: ingest a subset of prompts, run benchmarks for latency/cost, and validate routing and quotas. we'll propose a small dedicated pool for consistent results.
[00:08:43] Ben: what's the onboarding timeline? we have procurement steps - likely 3-4 weeks for a pilot contract.
[00:08:49] Olivia: that's common. we'll send a templated pilot agreement; engineering work can start in parallel with NDA.
[00:08:56] Priya: last question on encryption - do you support client-side encryption?
[00:09:01] Diego: we support envelope encryption with customer KMS for Dedicated/Private; client-side field encryption is doable but usually done client-side before sending. we'll put details in the security pack.
[00:09:14] Maya: great. can we recap next steps?
[00:09:18] Olivia: sure. Olivia will send pricing and hosted vs dedicated comparison; Diego will share LangChain/LlamaIndex repo and gateway proxy examples; Priya will send security requirements and we will schedule a POC kickoff once NDA is signed.
[00:09:33] Ben: timeline wise, we'll aim for the week of Dec 15 for kickoff.
[00:09:38] Olivia: perfect.
[00:09:40] Diego: I'll also add a quick benchmark plan - list of sample prompts, expected throughput, and p50/p95 targets.
[00:09:47] Maya: thanks folks.
[00:09:49] Olivia: thanks everyone, talk soon.
